_note: Hand-written task proposals for the commits after ebdf7a5 that yield gold-diff units (ADR-099 §2.3 source 1; review item 2's `task` conditioning and item 9's derived units). Written by the 2026-09-03 session from each commit's intent, before-the-fact in shape, with no line of the diff quoted; one per commit, matched to units by commit prefix.

task: Add a knowledge-only mode to hobbes-proxy so a host session on this repo can use the six read-only knowledge tools (who_calls, tests_guarding, graph_neighborhood, get_module_doc, list_invariants, list_blind_spots) without exec or reflect being registered at all — absent from the tool list, not refused at call time. Keep the flight log. Add a repo-level .mcp.json that starts the proxy this way, and cover the mode in the MCP tests.

Stand up an oracle-grading lane under bench/oracle as its own Go module: an `oracle` binary with `export` (Hobbes's call edges from a derived graph), `go-rta` (a reachability-based call graph over a Go zone, rooted at main and init so test mains reach their tests), and `grade` (confirm / contradict / miss per edge). Add a run-cell.sh that runs the three on a repo. Land it on fixture truth first: minigo and a new two-module fixture with one interface-dispatch call, with the export tests and a README describing the decisions.

Grade this repo's own Go zone with the RTA oracle and make the grader report recall by class of miss — reachability oracles over-approximate function values, so split misses into calls the site resolved versus calls through interfaces, function values and closures. Fix the match defect where generic instantiations were unwound differently by the two sides. Add a fixture module using generics to pin it.

Make the grader's miss record report classes as how-the-call-is-made × what-it-reaches (static / interface / func-value × named / closure), print each class's share of misses, and mark the classes a reachability oracle inflates. Test the class assignment.

Add a TypeScript oracle: grade a TS zone against the zone's own tsc (a small script under bench/oracle/ts that records what the checker resolved each call site to), wire it into the oracle binary and run-cell.sh, and extend export and grade for it. Resolve the first-pass contradictions that came from anonymous call signatures by a binding rule on the oracle side, report miss classes by the callee's declaration kind, and add the minits fixture self-test.

Write the oracle lane's own defect record into bench/oracle/README.md: every way the oracle itself has been wrong so far (H-1 through H-8), each with the symptom, the cell it appeared in, and its status.
Let `oracle export` exclude sub-trees (an --exclude flag, repeatable) so a monorepo's root cell can be graded without the nested modules, and have run-cell.sh pass the flag through.
Add a --no-tests flag to `oracle go-rta` so a root too large to load together with its test packages can still be graded from its non-test roots; record it as the fix for defect H-9.
Add a --packages flag to `oracle go-rta` restricting the loaded program to a subtree of packages, so a module too large to load whole can be graded cell by cell; part of H-9.

Grade dagger's Go modules with the RTA oracle module by module (the root module does not fit as one program). Mirror export's --exclude in go-rta so both sides see the same tree, and record the type-conversions-drawn-as-calls contradictions as an extraction defect handed to the extraction workstream, with the gorta tests extended for the new flags.

Fix the Go call edges the oracle lane found wrong or missing: a Go `calls` fact whose target is a type is a conversion and must project as `uses`; an expression operand is never a conversion candidate in the syntactic fallback (the name collision with a same-package type was dropping chain, left-hand-side and method-expression calls); a call of a generic function parsed as a conversion to a generic type is a call site; and a function's call to itself is an edge in both the projection and the Python fallback. Add a fixture covering the shapes and update the verification pins.
In the Go syntax provider, name a typed var or const spec by its name field rather than by its type — dagger showed 58 phantom symbols named after the string type. Add a regression test.

Add two more oracles to the lane: a Python trace oracle built on sys.monitoring that records, under the repo's own test suite, which callee each call site actually reached; and a Rust oracle that walks MIR through rustc_driver on a pinned nightly. Extend export for Python and Rust (package nodes; edges written by macros excluded), give the grader asymmetric buckets for a dynamic oracle (a call not exercised is not a contradiction) and the macro/generated miss classes, add py-trace and rust-mir subcommands and run-cell support, and use miniapp and minirust as the fixture self-tests. Move the verification pins for Python and Rust accordingly.

Veto two wrong shapes in the syntactic fallback that the trace and MIR oracles exposed: in Python, a bare name bound in a scope spanning the call site must never resolve to a module-level namesake (pytest fixture parameters were binding to the fixture function); in Rust, a macro invocation binds only to a macro symbol, never to a function of the same name. Surface the semantic sites whose target starts no symbol as a 'below-floor' tail class: project() reports them, coverage rows carry the floored count, the tail sums to unresolved plus floored, and list_blind_spots names it.

Add a poison check to `oracle grade`: re-target every Hobbes edge to a declaration the oracle never resolved that site to, and report how many the oracle refused, could not judge, or falsely confirmed — the last must be zero. Have run-cell.sh always run it, add fixture tests for all four oracle kinds, and make cell records carry a signed before → after line on regrade. Drop the two thin repos from the verification pins.

Fix the agent loop's discipline under window saturation: one fit per elide cycle; mutating and short tool results are never elided; an elided read revokes the path's edit ticket; no edit in the turn a path was first read; one bounded handoff nudge; a `handoff:` line on every unit record. Scope the duplicate-symbol record to the files' common directory and word it per lane, and have the SCIP helper report duplicates per lane.

Work through the oracle defect review's actions: guard descend() against unbounded recursion and add a watchdog; add the element-access call-site rule to the TS oracle (a site through a bracket index names the key); collapse membership checks into one predicate; represent a zone with no roots as an explicit state; emit [] rather than null for empty lists; label precision as a lower bound in reports. Add the minits lookup shapes as a fixture and update the graph fixture and grader tests.

Run every lane B (SCIP) step inside the sandbox image so repo-authored code never executes on the host: plan each step's mounts (cache root writable at its host path, the helper and its symlink targets read-only, hop by hop), no network for index steps, separate fetch containers for dependency downloads. Steps that execute repo code must refuse without containment via a distinct refusal type that every general catch names first; the others run on the host and say so. Keep a disclosed escape hatch via an environment variable.

Run the Python trace oracle and the Rust MIR oracle inside the sandbox image as well: a planner in bench/oracle/internal/contain shaping the mounts (the tree overlaid at its host path, the cell directory and Hobbes cache writable, the nightly sysroot / driver / tracer / interpreter read-only), no network for the trace run, a cargo-fetch container followed by an offline check for Rust. Route pytrace and rustmir through it, stamp exports and reports with the containment record, make the fixture self-tests run contained and skip without the image, and confirm the regrades are a numeric no-op.

Add `hobbes ingest --uncontained` that prints its disclosure first and sets the escape hatch; keep a ledger of every lane B step's containment and write it into graph.json as a containment stamp (steps, all_contained, escape_hatch); have the ingest summary and list_blind_spots name an artifact whose lane B ran on the host and stay silent when the guarantee held; print a knowledge-only banner at serve start that states the scope. Cover the stamp, the ledger and the banner in the CLI, knowledge and proxy tests.

Fix the four shapes the seven-cell triage found: the Go syntactic fallback must refuse a bare name that a local binding spans (the scope veto, Go shape); a Rust `calls` fact whose target is a type is a tuple-struct constructor and projects as `uses`; a call through a function-valued binding is graded abstract rather than contradicted (export carries the target kind); the Python tracer anchors an @overload implementation at the first stub's line. Add a func-value grader test and regrade.
Re-derive the §3.8 verification pins from the evidence rows so the verbatim-pin test in extract/verification.py is green again, and update the counts the test checks.

Close the two held harness defects: a planner whose handoff resolves to nothing is re-planned once, and under --coverage strict it is a plan error with its own status and a record naming what was unresolved; assignment then runs on the lexical seeds and says so. Track which seeds the proposal's text alone hit, drop such a seed from unit modules when it is a hub (fan-in ≥ 30), carry the reason into the spec, and make every-seed-a-lexical-hub a seed error that names --seed. A human's or the planner's seed on a hub stays work.

Have every artifact say which Hobbes built it: graph.json carries a built_by stamp (checkout, sha, dirty) of the pipeline code that ran, `hobbes ingest` prints it, every knowledge answer opens with it, and the proxy prints its own build revision at serve start. Start the knowledge proxy from the sandbox image via a launcher that refuses without podman or the image, with an environment variable that runs the host binary and says so. Cover the stamp, the header and the launcher in tests.

Add Java as the sixth language: a lane A syntax provider (overload-aware ids, an arity- and inheritance-aware fallback, anonymous members as local bindings, a JUnit test inventory), lane B via scip-java driven through the repo's own Maven or Gradle build inside the image with a network, the helper owning the SCIP typed-range decode, and the containment profile for the new steps. Teach the knowledge tools and the tail classes about Java, and extend the helper's node tests.

Build a Java oracle that is javac itself: a JDK-only javac plugin riding the repo's own build (a wrapping javac under Maven, an init script under Gradle) that records what the checker resolved each call site to, with declarations keyed across compilation shards and a dynamic site carrying its declared method plus the class-hierarchy override set. Wire java-javac into the oracle binary, contain it, add export and grade support and their tests, and give Java its §3.8 verification row.

Split Java lane B into two contained passes: a networked resolve pass that runs the build's own dependency resolution on a stage holding the build files and no .java sources (Maven with nothing to compile; Gradle with a resolve-all init script), then an offline index pass with scip-java attached on the full stage. Add the resolve profile and offline flags to containment, drive both passes from scipsource with a recorded failure not stopping the index, make the helper's Java build command offline, and move the profile pins and the Java grader and javac tests.

Make the Go syntactic fallback safe under build constraints: keep package-level declarations per (directory, name) with their package and their `//go:build` line or filename GOOS/GOARCH, resolve a split name only when exactly one declaration shares the caller's configuration, and otherwise abstain into a new build-tag-set tail class reported by the CLI and the knowledge tools. Have the scip-go record name the constrained files a one-configuration index left dark. Update the verification pins and add tests for the split-name shapes.
